steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mise en place means 'everything in its place' — preparing and organising all ingredients and equipment before cooking begins, ensuring efficient and safe food preparation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The bridge grip is used to hold food securely when cutting: form a bridge with thumb and fingers over the food, guiding the knife underneath. Used for cutting foods in half.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The claw grip is used for slicing and chopping: curl fingers inward like a claw, with fingertips behind the knuckles, guiding the knife while keeping fingers safe.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Knife types and uses: chef's knife (general chopping), paring knife (small precision work), bread knife (serrated for bread), filleting knife (flexible for fish), carving knife (slicing cooked meat).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Demonstrate knowledge of specific knife grips (bridge and claw) — these are frequently tested practical skills. When asked about weighing and measuring, emphasise accuracy and explain what happens if measurements are wrong. Safety questions require specific practices, not vague answers: name the grip, describe the technique, explain the precaution. Use French culinary terms where relevant (mise en place) to show technical knowledge.
